## Problem

`Terraform Drift` is red on `main` and has been on every recent run. The most recent
failure is run `35494675507` (`2026-09-20T06:36:37Z`). Every listed run in the last 10
has `conclusion: failure`.

The failure is a configuration-input error, not drift, not auth, not a state lock:

```
Error: No value for required variable
  on bedrock_spend_cap.tf line 31:
  31: variable "bedrock_daily_cap_usd" {

The root module input variable "bedrock_daily_cap_usd" is not set, and has no
default value.
```

The same error repeats for `bedrock_warn_threshold_usd` (line 44),
`bedrock_cap_seed_rates` (line 52) and `bedrock_cap_unknown_rate_per_1k` (line 63).

## Root cause

`infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf` declares 4 variables with no `default`, and
nothing supplies them. Two of the declarations carry a description asserting the value
is "supplied outside the public tree", but no such supply mechanism was ever built:

- `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml` passes no `TF_VAR_*` and no `-var-file`. Its
  only AWS inputs are the OIDC role `arn:aws:iam::896586841071:role/rebar-terraform-plan`
  (line 112) and region `us-east-1` (line 113).
- `infra/terraform/` contains no `terraform.tfvars`, no `*.auto.tfvars`, and no
  `*.tfvars` of any kind.
- No workflow anywhere in `.github/workflows/` references `TF_VAR_`.

So the variables were authored expecting an external supply that does not exist. The
plan therefore cannot run at all, which is why the job fails before reaching drift
detection.

## The values are measured, not guessed

All 4 are recoverable read-only from the deployed resources, so no value below is
inferred:

- `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name bedrock-spend-cap` returns
  `THRESHOLD_USD=500`, `WARN_THRESHOLD_USD=300`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K=0.075`, and the
  `SEED_RATES` map.
- `aws budgets describe-budgets` returns `BudgetName: bedrock-daily-500`,
  `BudgetLimit.Amount: 500.0`, `TimeUnit: DAILY`, `CostFilters.Service: Amazon Bedrock`.

`bedrock_daily_cap_usd` feeds both the budget limit and the budget *name*
(`bedrock-daily-%s`, `bedrock_spend_cap.tf:214-218`), so a wrong value would change the
budget's identity and not merely its threshold. `500` is confirmed correct by the live
budget name, which removes that risk rather than accepting it.

## None of the 4 is secret

`bedrock_cap_seed_rates` holds published Bedrock per-token list prices — the
declaration's own description calls them "Published Bedrock per-token rates". The other
3 are account-level spend-policy numbers. There is no credential among them, so the
public-tree concern is not disclosure.

The established repository pattern reinforces this split: AWS SSM under `/rebar/prod/*`
holds secrets (`infra/terraform/ssm.tf:2-6`, `scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:7-21`), while
non-secret CI configuration uses Actions `vars.*`. None of the 4 Bedrock values is in
SSM today.

## Design

Give each of the 4 variables a `default` in `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf` set
to its measured live value. This is the only option that keeps a local `terraform plan`
runnable without AWS-side configuration, and it adds no plan-time data dependency.

Rejected: `TF_VAR_*` from Actions secrets — nothing here is secret, and it would make
local planning impossible. Rejected: `data "aws_ssm_parameter"` — that pattern exists
for secrets, and using it here buys no secrecy while adding a plan-time AWS read.

Because the declarations currently assert the values come from outside the public tree,
that prose becomes false the moment defaults land. Both descriptions are corrected in
the same change so the module does not carry a claim its own code contradicts.

## Verification

The change is correct only if it produces **no** resource changes. Proven by

```
terraform -chdir=infra/terraform plan -input=false -lock=false -detailed-exitcode
```

exiting `0`, which is Terraform's "succeeded, no diff" code; exit `2` would mean the
defaults disagree with deployed state and the change is wrong. Repository gates are
proven by `make lint` and `make typecheck`, each exiting zero, and by `make test`
passing any test that asserts on this module.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bedrock_daily_cap_usd` declares a default of `500`.
- [ ] `bedrock_warn_threshold_usd` declares a default of `300`.
- [ ] `bedrock_cap_unknown_rate_per_1k` declares a default of `0.075`.
- [ ] `bedrock_cap_seed_rates` declares a default matching the deployed `SEED_RATES` map exactly.
- [ ] The `bedrock_warn_threshold_usd` description no longer claims the value is supplied outside the public tree.
- [ ] The `bedrock_cap_seed_rates` description no longer claims the value is supplied outside the public tree.
- [ ] `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform validate` exits zero.
- [ ] `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform plan -input=false -lock=false -detailed-exitcode` exits `0`, proving no resource diff.
- [ ] The `Terraform Drift` workflow run on the change reports success.
